channel.title: planet — Essays on where systems tip
channel.description: planet – essays on tipping points, hysteresis and emergence in climate, politics, technology and markets. An offshoot of emergenz.art.

item.title: Is something tipping here?
item.description: The slump in AI stocks after the 2026 US midterms, tested against the hallmarks of a tipping point. Sandpiles, reflexivity, coupled tipping points and hysteresis: what the post-election crash reveals about tipping points – and what it does not.

item.title: The threshold no one sees
item.description: An essay on artificial intelligence, emergence and the question of whether there is a tipping point. On abilities nobody programmed, jumps inside neural networks and the question of whether AGI is a tipping point.

item.title: Two clocks
item.description: An essay on climate policy, tipping points and responsibility for processes that outlast a legislative term. The political clock measures legislative terms, the climate clock centuries. On compromises physics does not recognise, and on responsibility.

item.title: The way back is a different one
item.description: An essay on hysteresis, attractors and the memory of complex systems. Why a system that has tipped does not return when the cause disappears – from clear lakes to ice sheets to societies.

item.title: The conveyor belt dies quietly
item.description: An essay on the AMOC, the physics of irreversibility and the failure of linear thinking. The Atlantic overturning circulation is weakening. Early warning signs, hysteresis, and a policy that dismantles its own instruments.
